title: Asking questions
description: Ask what, who, where, when, why, how and how much, and turn any statement into a yes/no question.

guide.title: Question words stay in place
guide.text:
English moves the question word to the front. Bengali leaves it where the answer would go, which is normally just before the verb.

আপনি কোথায় যাচ্ছেন? - 'you where are-going?' The answer drops into the same slot: আমি বাজারে যাচ্ছি।

The main question words:
কী (kee) what
কে (ke) who - কার (kaar) whose - কাকে (kaake) whom, to whom
কোথায় (kothaay) where
কখন (kokhon) when, at what time - কবে (kobe) when, on what day
কেন (keno) why
কেমন (kemon) how, what like
কোন (kon) which
কত (koto) how much
কী করে (kee kore) or কীভাবে (keebhaabe) how, in what way

Most of them begin with ক, just as English ones begin with wh-. In কেন and কেমন the e is the a of 'cat'.

guide.title: Yes/no questions: কি with a short i
guide.text:
To ask a yes/no question, you can simply say the statement with a rising tone: আপনি বাঙালি? 'You are Bengali?'

Or you can add the little word কি (ki), usually right after the subject: আপনি কি বাঙালি? It has no meaning of its own; it only announces that a yes/no question is coming, like 'do' or 'is' at the start of an English question.

This কি is spelt with the SHORT vowel sign. The word for 'what', কী, is spelt with the LONG one. They sound almost the same (কী carries the stress), but in writing the difference matters:

আপনি কি খাবেন? - Will you eat? (yes or no)
আপনি কী খাবেন? - What will you eat?

To answer, repeat the verb: খাব (I will) or খাব না (I won't).

guide.title: How much and how many
guide.text:
কত (koto) asks for an amount or a number: কত টাকা? 'how much money?'; কত দূর? 'how far?'. It is also the word for asking any number - a price, a phone number, a date, someone's age: আপনার বয়স কত? 'what is your age?'

For counting things, add the classifier: কটা (kotaa) 'how many (things)', কজন (kojon) 'how many (people)'. These are often written ক'টা and ক'জন, or in full কয়টা, কয়জন.

কটা is also how you ask the time: কটা বাজে?

guide.title: Checking: তো and না
guide.text:
Two small words turn a statement into 'isn't it?' or 'won't you?'.

তো (to) at the end of a sentence expects the answer yes: আপনি চা খাবেন তো? 'You'll have tea, won't you?'; ভালো তো? 'All well, I hope?'

তাই না? (taai naa), literally 'so, no?', is the general tag 'isn't that so?'.

না (naa) alone at the end also works as a tag: খুব গরম, না? 'Very hot, isn't it?'

phrases.note: কী with the long vowel sign means 'what'.
কখন asks for a time of day; কবে (kobe) asks for a day or date.
টাকা is the rupee in India and the taka in Bangladesh, and also simply 'money'.
কী করে, 'doing what', is the everyday 'how'.
কি with the short vowel sign only marks a yes/no question.
Bengali 'eats' tea, water and all other drinks.
